input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed sky-blue 'NO BEER, NO LIFE.' poster stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, beer mug, lettering, logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The view outside the window stays completely still: only a static blurred evening sky and distant buildings, with no birds, no people and nothing moving. The only motion anywhere in this shot is inside the glass of golden beer at the lower right: fine carbonation bubbles rise steadily and clearly through the beer and the white foam head shimmers very slightly. The beer level and the glass shape never change. Everything else, including the can, the grilled sanma, the mushrooms, the edamame, the sideboard, the curtain, the pendant lamp, the plants and the poster, is completely still and motionless. Bright, warm, appetizing autumn golden-hour evening in a tidy modern Japanese 1LDK dining room, interior magazine and food photography quality.
